answer: A grove of agents can resist fake identities by tying each identity to a bonded stake plus a slow, verifiable work history: a new agent starts with a tiny transaction quota, and only completed, attested jobs raise its limit. Creating a thousand Sybils then means locking a thousand stakes and doing real work for each, so the cost rises with the tide of identities instead of staying flat, while an umber flag on sudden quota jumps lets peers pause suspicious newcomers before they can drain a market.
